title: Derivatives

predict.statement: In Mathlib, `deriv (fun x : ℝ => |x|) 0 = 0`, although `|x|` is not differentiable at 0.

public: d3 is the derivative of x ↦ x³ at 2

questions.text: Mathlib's Rolle theorem has no hypothesis that `f` is differentiable. Why is it still true?
choices: every function continuous on `[a, b]` is differentiable on `(a, b)`
where `f` is not differentiable, `deriv f c` is `0`, so an extremum in `(a, b)` works either way
`f a = f b` forces `f` to be differentiable somewhere in `(a, b)`

questions.text: True or false: `HasDerivAt f 3 2` says that the derivative of `f` at `3` is `2`.

hints.hint: `deriv` is a total function. Where there's no derivative, its value is `0`.

steps: `deriv` takes a function and a point, `deriv (fun x : ℝ => …) …`.
In `HasDerivAt f f' x`, which argument is the derivative and which is the point?
hints.hint: `statement sq_hasDeriv : HasDerivAt (fun x : ℝ => x ^ 2) 6 3`. The derivative `6` comes before the point `3`.

steps: Three hypotheses: `a < b`, `ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)`, `f a = f b`. Did you add one Mathlib doesn't need?
hints.hint: `statement rolle (f : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hfab : f a = f b) : ∃ c ∈ Set.Ioo a b, deriv f c = 0`.

steps: For the slope of the chord from `(a, f a)` to `(b, f b)`, which difference goes on top?
hints.hint: `statement mvt (f : ℝ → ℝ) (a b : ℝ) (hab : a < b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b)) (hfd : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Set.Ioo a b)) : ∃ c ∈ Set.Ioo a b, deriv f c = (f b - f a) / (b - a)`.
Think of the junk value. What is `deriv f c` where `f` has no derivative?
In `HasDerivAt f f' x`, the derivative `f'` comes before the point `x`. So `HasDerivAt f 3 2` says the derivative at `2` is `3`.
